name: ML / AI engineering
blurb: A rare all-rounder: decent entry, fast climb, livable hours and the AI-skills premium underneath it.

route.summary: Numerate degree + MSc, or self-taught portfolio via a data/software role, then a crossover.
steps: Python, SQL, ML fundamentals and a cloud platform
MSc in AI/Data Science, or a strong public project portfolio
Data/software role, then migrate into ML/AI engineering
route.alt: Direct entry to junior ML roles is rare; most cross in from an adjacent role.

name: Data engineering
blurb: The backbone of modern data, one of the few high-paying tracks you can enter on a portfolio.

route.summary: Portfolio-first or MSc conversion into a junior data/analytics engineer role.
steps: Junior data engineer or analytics engineer
route.alt: Conversion MSc is the common route for non-numerate graduates.

name: Data science
blurb: Statistics and ML applied to business questions, higher maths bar, and squeezed between analysts and ML engineers.

route.summary: Numerate degree → MSc (often) → analyst or junior data scientist.
steps: Maths, stats, CS, economics or science
Data analyst or junior data scientist
route.alt: Analyst-to-scientist internal moves happen without a master’s.

name: Data analyst
blurb: The most accessible data role and a springboard into science or engineering, the routine reporting end is in AI’s sights.

route.summary: Any numerate-ish degree or self-study → analyst role → specialise.
steps: SQL, Excel, a BI tool, some Python
Senior analyst, or pivot to data science/engineering
route.alt: Bootcamps and certifications are a common route in.

name: Software eng (generalist)
blurb: Well-paid and quick to climb, but the junior rung is the most AI-exposed spot here.

route.summary: Degree, bootcamp or self-taught portfolio → junior developer.
steps: A language, projects on GitHub, fundamentals
Junior developer, grad scheme or apprenticeship
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships and bootcamps are well-established routes.

name: DevOps / cloud engineer
blurb: The infrastructure-automation backbone of software, usually reached from software or sysadmin, not entered cold.

route.summary: Software/sysadmin base → cloud certs → DevOps engineer.
steps: Software dev or systems administration experience
route.alt: Rarely a first job; a step up from an adjacent role.

name: Cybersecurity engineering
blurb: Structural shortage, rising demand, contract optionality, a durable, well-paid all-rounder.

route.summary: Degree, apprenticeship, bootcamp or certs → analyst → engineer.
route.alt: Cyber degree apprenticeships are strong low-debt routes.

name: UX / UI designer
blurb: Design plus research plus psychology, better paid and more durable than pure graphic design.

route.summary: Portfolio + (optional) course → junior UX → specialise.
steps: UX process, research, prototyping; case studies
route.alt: Conversion from graphic design, research or front-end dev.

name: IT support technician
blurb: A very open on-ramp into tech with clear progression into networks, cloud or security.

route.summary: Certs/apprenticeship → help desk → specialise up.
steps: Network, cloud, security or sysadmin roles
route.alt: One of the most accessible entries into the whole tech sector.

name: Product manager
blurb: Decides what gets built and why, strong pay and a path to leadership, but hard to enter cold.

route.summary: Lateral move from engineering, analytics, consulting or an APM scheme.
steps: Engineering, data, UX, consulting or marketing
APM scheme or internal move to junior PM
PM → senior PM → group PM / director
route.alt: APM graduate schemes are the direct route, but very competitive.

name: Quant finance / dev
blurb: The highest ceiling here, and the thinnest durability: elite entry, boom-bust cycles, burnout baked in.

route.summary: Elite numerate degree, often a PhD/MSc → quant analyst/dev.
steps: Quant analyst, dev or researcher at a fund/bank
route.alt: Strong CS + competitive programming into quant dev without a PhD.

name: Investment banking (IBD)
blurb: Among the highest early pay anywhere, and the worst hours here, with a brutal analyst-to-MD tournament.

route.summary: Target-uni degree → internship pipeline → analyst programme.
route.alt: A master’s in finance helps non-target candidates.

name: Management consulting
blurb: Broad exposure and an exit-opportunity machine, at the cost of relentless travel and hours.

route.summary: Strong degree → case-interview recruitment → analyst/associate.
steps: Case + fit interviews are the gate
route.alt: Post-MBA entry, or experienced hire from industry.

name: Financial analyst
blurb: Corporate finance or markets analysis, a gateway to senior finance, with routine modelling automating.

route.summary: Degree → graduate role → often CFA while working.
route.alt: Accountancy or MBA routes into corporate finance.

name: Chartered accountancy (ACA)
blurb: The reliable escalator into senior finance and the CFO track.

route.summary: Degree + graduate scheme with ACA/ACCA exams → chartered.
route.alt: School-leaver and apprenticeship routes (AAT → ACA) skip the degree.

name: Auditor
blurb: A structured, secure route through the profession, but the routine testing half is heavily automation-exposed.

route.summary: Degree → audit graduate scheme with ACA → qualify → industry or stay.
steps: Audit graduate role at a firm
ACA → senior auditor, or exit to industry
route.alt: Apprenticeship routes into audit are growing.

name: HR manager
blurb: A stable, people-centred profession with a ladder into leadership, middling pay, admin-heavy tasks automating.

route.summary: Any degree → HR role → CIPD qualification → manager.
route.alt: Apprenticeships and internal moves from admin roles.

name: Recruitment consultant
blurb: Very open entry and uncapped commission make top earnings high, but target-driven, cyclical and insecure.

route.summary: Any background → trainee consultant → build a desk.
steps: Trainee consultant, drive matters more than a degree
Develop a sector niche; hit targets
Senior/principal, team lead, or start an agency
route.alt: In-house recruitment offers steadier, salaried work.

name: Economist
blurb: Analytical policy or commercial work with strong credibility, usually needs a strong quantitative postgrad.

route.summary: Economics degree → MSc (often) → government/consultancy/finance.
steps: Economics master’s expected for many roles
Government Economic Service, consultancy or finance
route.alt: The Government Economic Service fast stream is a key entry.

name: Insurance underwriter
blurb: A stable, less-visible profession pricing risk, good balance and security, with data tools reshaping the routine end.

route.summary: Any degree → trainee underwriter → CII qualifications.
steps: Senior underwriter → specialist lines or management
route.alt: Apprenticeships and internal moves from broking.

name: Doctor (GP / consultant)
blurb: The classic delayed-gratification curve: a punishing decade, then near-total security and strong money.

route.summary: Medical school → foundation → specialty training → consultant/GP.
steps: 3-8 yrs specialty/GP training → consultant or GP
route.alt: Graduate-entry medicine for those with a prior degree.

name: Surgeon
blurb: The apex of procedural medicine: elite pay and near-total security, at the cost of the longest training path here.

route.summary: Medical school → foundation → core → specialty surgical training → consultant.
steps: Higher surgical training → CCT → consultant surgeon
route.alt: Sub-specialisation and private practice raise earnings further.

name: Psychiatrist
blurb: Medicine’s security and pay applied to mental health, long training, but strong demand and better balance than surgery.

route.summary: Medical school → foundation → core + higher psychiatry training → consultant.
steps: Core + higher specialty training → consultant psychiatrist
route.alt: A range of sub-specialties (forensic, child, old-age).

name: Dentistry
blurb: Medicine’s pay and durability, but you can own the practice and reach the money faster.

route.summary: Dental school → foundation training → dentist (NHS/private/own practice).
steps: Associate → principal / practice owner, or specialise
route.alt: Specialty training (orthodontics, oral surgery) for higher earnings.

name: Registered nurse
blurb: Deep, durable demand and near-total security, modest banded pay and demanding shifts the trade-off.

route.summary: Nursing degree → NMC registration → band 5 nurse.
route.alt: Nursing degree apprenticeship, earn while you train.

name: Midwife
blurb: Deeply meaningful, automation-proof and utterly secure, modest banded pay and hard shifts the trade-off.

route.summary: Midwifery degree → NMC registration → practise.
route.alt: Shortened programmes for registered nurses.

name: Physiotherapist
blurb: Hands-on, trust-based and automation-resistant, with private-practice independence, capped ceiling the trade-off.

route.summary: Physio degree → HCPC registration → practise (NHS or private).
steps: NHS bands or a private practice
route.alt: Physiotherapy degree apprenticeship route.

name: Occupational therapist
blurb: Trust-based rehabilitation, automation-resistant with private options, a modest ceiling the cost of the meaning.

route.summary: OT degree → HCPC registration → practise.
route.alt: Degree apprenticeship route.

name: Radiographer
blurb: A stable, technical clinical role, AI assists imaging but the hands-on, patient-facing core endures.

route.summary: Radiography degree → HCPC registration → practise.
route.alt: Degree apprenticeship routes exist.

name: Pharmacist
blurb: Secure, well-regulated and clinically respected, with community-ownership options.

route.summary: MPharm → foundation year → registration assessment → registered pharmacist.
route.alt: Now includes prescribing from qualification under newer standards.

name: Optometrist
blurb: A clinical profession with strong high-street demand and practice-ownership upside, a competitive degree the barrier.

route.summary: Optometry degree → pre-reg year → GOC registration.
steps: GOC registration → practise, specialise or own a practice
route.alt: Independent-prescribing qualifications extend the clinical scope.

name: Veterinarian
blurb: Vocation-heavy and automation-proof with ownership upside, but a punishing degree and emotional toll.

route.summary: Vet degree → RCVS registration → practise.
steps: Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons registration
route.alt: Graduate-entry accelerated vet degrees for science graduates.

name: Clinical psychologist
blurb: Deeply meaningful and automation-resistant, with private-practice independence, the doctorate route is long and competitive.

route.summary: Psychology degree → experience → funded DClinPsy → HCPC registration.
route.cost: Doctorate often funded but hard to win
route.alt: Counselling psychology or PWP roles as faster entry.

name: Mental-health therapist
blurb: Rising demand, a deep trust-moat against automation, and private practice you own, modest ceiling the cost.

route.summary: Relevant degree + accredited training and placement hours → accredited.
route.alt: IAPT/PWP roles offer a faster, funded entry.

name: Paramedic
blurb: Embodied, high-responsibility and automation-proof, with expanding advanced-practice roles.

route.summary: Paramedic science degree → HCPC registration → practise.
steps: Ambulance service → advanced paramedic, GP roles
route.alt: Paramedic degree apprenticeship.

name: Care worker
blurb: Utterly automation-proof and always in demand, and the most open door in healthcare, but among the lowest pay here.

route.summary: Apply directly → on-the-job training → optional qualifications.
steps: Apply directly, no formal qualifications needed
Senior carer, then into nursing or management with study
route.alt: A common stepping stone into nursing via an apprenticeship.

name: Social worker
blurb: Demanding, meaningful, automation-proof frontline work with strong security, heavy caseloads and modest pay the reality.

route.summary: Social work degree (or apprenticeship) → registration → practise.
route.alt: Frontline/Step Up fast-track and apprenticeship routes.

name: Actuary
blurb: An exam gauntlet gates a near-recession-proof, comfortable, sane-hours career. Security is its superpower.

route.summary: Numerate degree → trainee role → professional exams → qualify.
route.alt: Actuarial apprenticeships offer a non-degree route.

name: Solicitor (corporate)
blurb: Superb pay and prestige, bought with the worst hours here and an up-or-out tournament.

route.summary: Degree (or conversion) + SQE → qualifying work experience → solicitor.
steps: Law degree, or any degree + conversion
2 yrs qualifying work experience → solicitor → partner
route.alt: Solicitor apprenticeships (6 yrs) qualify with no tuition debt.

name: Barrister
blurb: Advocacy at the top of the profession, self-employed and high-ceiling, but a brutally competitive route and precarious early years.

route.summary: Law degree/conversion → Bar course → pupillage → tenancy.
steps: Law degree or any degree + conversion
Vocational Bar training + join an Inn
Win a pupillage → tenancy in chambers
route.alt: Employed barrister roles (CPS, in-house) offer more security.

name: Paralegal
blurb: An accessible entry into law without the debt, but the routine document work is squarely in AI’s path.

route.summary: Any degree or paralegal qualification → paralegal role → optional route to solicitor.
steps: Law degree, or a paralegal qualification
Paralegal in a firm or in-house team
Senior paralegal, or qualify as a solicitor via SQE
route.alt: A common stepping stone toward qualifying as a solicitor.

name: Chartered surveyor
blurb: A stable, chartered profession across property, construction and land, with an inspection element that resists automation.

route.summary: RICS-accredited degree (or conversion) → APC → MRICS.
steps: RICS-accredited degree, or a conversion master’s
Pass the APC to become MRICS
route.alt: Surveying degree apprenticeships and conversion routes.

name: Town planner
blurb: Stable, meaningful shaping of the built environment with good balance, a modest ceiling outside senior private-sector roles.

route.summary: RTPI-accredited degree (or conversion) → APC → chartered planner.
steps: RTPI-accredited degree, or a conversion master’s
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships in planning are growing.

name: Civil / structural engineer
blurb: Infrastructure demand is structural, the work is embodied and accountable, and chartership is a durable moat.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate role → chartership (CEng).
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships lead to the same chartership.

name: Mechanical engineer
blurb: A broad, durable engineering discipline across manufacturing, energy and product, a solid, not spectacular, ceiling.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate role → chartership (CEng).
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships lead to the same chartership.

name: Electrical / electronics engineer
blurb: Power, electronics and embedded systems, riding electrification and defence demand, chartership a durable credential.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate role → chartership (CEng).
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships; strong defence and energy overlap.

name: Aerospace engineer
blurb: High-skill design and systems work in aviation, space and defence, cyclical, but clearance-gated roles are well protected.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate scheme → chartership (CEng).
steps: Often at a defence or aerospace prime
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships at major aerospace employers.

name: Research scientist (academia)
blurb: Intellectually rich frontier work, but a broken labour market, low pay for the training, and brutal postdoc-to-lecturer odds.

route.summary: Degree → PhD → postdoc(s) → (rare) permanent academic post.
route.cost: PhD often funded, but long low-pay years
steps: Postdoc years → compete for scarce lecturer roles
route.alt: Industry R&D pays far better and is far more secure than academia.

name: Biomedical / lab scientist
blurb: Steady, essential lab work underpinning healthcare and research, secure and balanced, with a modest ceiling.

route.summary: Accredited degree → HCPC registration → practise (NHS or industry).
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships and the NHS Scientist Training Programme.

name: Environmental scientist
blurb: Growing demand from climate, energy and regulation, meaningful and durable, though pay lags outside senior consultancy.

route.summary: Science degree → graduate role → chartership (CEnv/CSci).
route.alt: MSc in a specialism (e.g. sustainability) aids entry.

name: Airline pilot (senior)
blurb: Great once senior, but a huge self-funded training bill, a cyclical industry, and a life lived on a roster.

route.summary: Self-funded training or cadetship → frozen ATPL → first officer.
steps: First officer → captain with hours and seniority
route.alt: Airline cadet schemes reduce or spread the upfront cost.

name: Air traffic controller
blurb: Unusually high pay for a non-degree route, with strong security and a hard automation moat, brutal selection the barrier.

route.summary: Aptitude selection → paid training → validation → controller.
steps: Rigorous aptitude testing, most are filtered out
route.alt: No degree needed; age and medical requirements apply.

name: Train driver
blurb: Unusually high pay for the entry bar, strongly unionised and secure, but limited progression and few operators.

route.summary: Apply to a trainee scheme → paid training → qualified driver.
steps: Trainee driver scheme, competitive, no degree
Paid rules, traction and route training
Qualified driver; limited but stable progression
route.alt: Often entered from other rail roles (conductor, station staff).

name: Electrician
blurb: High-demand, licensed and riding the EV/solar/heat-pump boom, arguably the most future-proof trade, with strong self-employment upside.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ Level 3 → qualified electrician (→ self-employed).
steps: Earn while you learn toward NVQ Level 3
AM2 assessment + Part P; join a competent-person scheme
route.alt: Adult fast-track courses exist, but employers value logged experience.

name: Plumber
blurb: Essential, embodied and impossible to offshore, with excellent self-employment earnings, call-outs and emergency hours the trade-off.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ Level 2/3 → qualified plumber (gas optional).
steps: Level 3; add Gas Safe for boiler work
route.alt: Gas Safe registration significantly raises earning power.

name: Gas / heating engineer
blurb: Gas Safe registration is a licence to earn, high demand, strong self-employed rates, and heat-pump work adding a green tailwind.

route.summary: Plumbing/heating route → Gas Safe registration → engineer.
steps: Plumbing & heating apprenticeship or managed programme
Domestic/commercial work, or run a business
route.alt: Managed Learning Programmes for adult career-changers.

name: Carpenter / joiner
blurb: A craft trade spanning construction and bespoke joinery, hands-on and automation-proof, a solid ceiling with real ownership potential.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ → carpenter/joiner (→ own business).
steps: Site carpentry or bench joinery NVQ
First/second fix, joinery, or run a firm
route.alt: College diplomas plus experience, though apprenticeship is preferred.

name: Welder / fabricator
blurb: A certification-gated trade where coded (offshore/pipeline) welders earn very well, physically demanding and site-dependent.

route.summary: Apprenticeship/college → welding certifications → coded welder.
steps: Offshore, pipeline or fabrication for top rates
route.alt: Coded/specialist welding pays a large premium over general work.

name: Bricklayer
blurb: Core construction trade, embodied and hard to automate, with self-employed earnings, weather-exposed and physically tough.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ → bricklayer (→ self-employed/gang).
route.alt: College courses plus site experience.

name: Painter & decorator
blurb: One of the most accessible trades to enter and go solo, a lower ceiling and easy competition the trade-off.

route.summary: Apprenticeship or short course → experience → self-employed.
steps: Experience and a portfolio of jobs
route.alt: Very common self-taught → self-employed route.

name: Auto mechanic / technician
blurb: A hands-on trade shifting fast to EV and diagnostics, retrain for EVs and durability rises; stick to petrol and it falls.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ → technician (→ EV specialism / own garage).
steps: EV/hybrid diagnostics, or open a garage
route.alt: EV/hybrid certification is the future-proofing move.

name: Chef
blurb: A hands-on craft that’s automation-resistant with restaurant-ownership upside, brutal hours and low early pay the cost.

route.summary: Kitchen entry (+ optional college) → work up the brigade → head chef.
steps: Head chef, or open your own place
route.alt: Apprenticeships and culinary school speed the early climb.

name: Personal trainer
blurb: Quick and cheap to qualify, highly independent and people-facing, but client-dependent and insecure, especially early.

route.summary: Level 2/3 certification → build a client base → self-employed.
steps: Level 2 Gym Instructor + Level 3 Personal Trainer
Gym floor → grow a client base
Independent, online coaching, or own studio
route.alt: Online coaching and niche specialisms raise the ceiling.

name: Teaching
blurb: AI-resistant in the relational sense and secure, but a flat, publicly-set pay scale and heavy workload cap it here.

route.summary: Degree + teaching qualification (PGCE/QTS) → qualified teacher.
steps: Subject degree, or an education degree
route.alt: Salaried school-based training and apprenticeship routes.

name: University lecturer
blurb: Prestige, autonomy and intellectual freedom, undercut by a difficult labour market and years of insecure early posts.

route.summary: Degree → PhD → postdoc/teaching → permanent lectureship.
route.cost: PhD often funded; long lean years
steps: Postdoc, teaching fellow, or research fellow
Compete for a permanent academic post → senior lecturer/professor
route.alt: Teaching-focused and industry-adjacent academic roles.

name: Civil servant (Fast Stream)
blurb: Stable, meaningful public-policy work with good balance and a clear ladder into leadership, pay lags the private sector.

route.summary: Degree → Fast Stream assessment centre → leadership scheme.
steps: Rotational scheme → Grade 7 → senior civil service
route.alt: Direct-entry apprenticeships and standard grades.

name: Police officer
blurb: Secure, pensioned public service with genuine variety and progression, shift work and public scrutiny the trade-offs.

route.summary: Degree-entry or degree-holder entry → probation → constable.
steps: PCDA apprenticeship, degree-holder entry, or pre-join degree
route.alt: Direct-entry detective routes exist.

name: Firefighter
blurb: Embodied, respected public service with a strong pension and security, very competitive to enter and physically demanding.

route.summary: Fitness + aptitude selection → training → firefighter.
steps: Physical, aptitude and medical tests, very competitive
route.alt: On-call (retained) firefighter routes alongside other work.

name: Architect
blurb: Creative and respected, with ownership potential, but one of the longest, lowest-paid qualification routes for the effort.

route.summary: Part 1 → Part 2 → Part 3, ~7 years to registration.
steps: 2-yr MArch after a year in practice
route.alt: Architecture apprenticeships offer an earn-while-you-train route.

name: Interior designer
blurb: Creative and ownership-friendly, with high-end residential and commercial upside, project-based income and some AI pressure the risks.

route.summary: Degree or course + portfolio → junior/assistant → own studio.
steps: Interior design degree or diploma; build a portfolio
route.alt: Self-taught + portfolio route into residential work.

name: Digital marketing manager
blurb: Accessible and creative with freelance/agency upside, but generative AI is reshaping content and campaign work fast.

route.summary: Any degree or none → junior/exec role → build a results portfolio.
steps: SEO, paid media, analytics, content, often self-taught + certs
Manager → head of marketing, or freelance
route.alt: Bootcamps and platform certifications speed entry.

name: Journalist
blurb: Meaningful and varied, but a shrinking, insecure industry with modest pay and heavy AI/economic pressure on the routine end.

route.summary: Degree or NCTJ → junior reporter → build a beat.
steps: Journalism degree or NCTJ; build clips
route.alt: Portfolio + freelancing route without formal qualifications.

name: Copywriter
blurb: Flexible, creative and freelance-friendly, but generative AI is compressing routine copy hard, so the safe ground is strategy and brand.

route.summary: Portfolio → junior/agency role or freelance → specialise.
steps: Spec work and a portfolio; degree optional
route.alt: Move toward brand/content strategy to stay ahead of AI.

name: Photographer
blurb: Creative and independent with full ownership, but income is project-based and volatile, and AI imagery pressures commercial work.

route.summary: Build a portfolio → assist/second-shoot → own business.
steps: Develop a style and body of work; kit
Weddings, commercial, editorial or fine-art niche
route.alt: Salaried in-house/commercial roles offer more stability.

name: Graphic designer
blurb: Creative and portfolio-driven, but among the most AI-exposed careers here, with tools compressing routine work and pay.

route.summary: Build a portfolio (degree optional) → junior designer → specialise or freelance.
steps: Design tools and a strong portfolio
route.alt: Moving toward UX/product design improves pay and durability.

name: Estate agent
blurb: Very open entry with commission-driven upside and agency-ownership potential, but cyclical and target-heavy.

route.summary: Any background → negotiator role → build commission → branch/own agency.
steps: Valuer, branch manager, or open an agency
route.alt: Lettings and commercial property as alternative specialisms.

name: Content creation / influencing
blurb: Anyone can start and you own everything, but this is the rare winner’s curve; the median attempt earns almost nothing.

route.summary: Just start, build an audience and monetise. No barrier, low odds.
route.time: Immediate to start; years to earn (if ever)
steps: Pick a platform and niche; publish consistently
Build an audience, the hard, uncertain part
Ads, sponsorship, products, for the minority who scale
route.alt: Video, writing or design skills transfer to paid roles as a fallback.

name: Business analyst
blurb: The bridge between business needs and technical delivery, stable and well-paid, though the routine requirements-gathering end is increasingly tool-assisted.

route.summary: Any degree or an internal move → BA role → BCS/agile certification.
steps: Process mapping, stakeholder skills, some SQL
Junior BA, or a sideways move from operations/analysis
Senior BA → lead → product or delivery roles
route.alt: BCS Business Analysis certifications; a common internal move from ops.

name: Mobile developer
blurb: Builds the apps everyone lives on, strong pay and demand, though cross-platform tools and AI assistants are squeezing routine work.

route.summary: Portfolio of published apps (degree optional) → junior mobile dev.
steps: Swift/Kotlin or React Native; publish an app
route.alt: Bootcamps and degree apprenticeships are common routes.

name: Game developer
blurb: Creative and passion-driven, blending code and art, but long hours, volatile studios and fierce competition are the trade-offs.

route.summary: CS or games degree + portfolio → junior developer at a studio.
steps: C++/C#, Unreal or Unity; ship a game or demo
route.alt: Modding, game jams and indie releases build the portfolio.

name: QA / test engineer
blurb: Guards software quality through manual and automated testing, an accessible route into tech, though automation is reshaping the manual end.

route.summary: Entry via a testing role → automation skills → QA engineer.
steps: Test cases, bug tracking, a scripting language
route.alt: ISTQB certification and bootcamps ease entry.

name: Network engineer
blurb: Designs and maintains the networks everything runs on, stable, certification-driven, and a solid bridge toward cloud and security.

route.summary: Certifications/apprenticeship → support → network engineer.
route.alt: IT apprenticeships lead straight into networking.

name: Solutions architect
blurb: Designs how large technical systems fit together, among the best-paid tech roles, reached with years of engineering experience rather than entered cold.

route.summary: Senior engineering experience → architecture role → certification.
steps: Years as a software or cloud engineer
route.alt: Pre-sales and consulting architect tracks exist.

name: Technical writer
blurb: Turns complex products into clear documentation, calm, remote-friendly work, though generative AI is a real pressure on routine docs.

route.summary: Writing plus technical aptitude → junior technical writer.
steps: Clear doc samples; learn a docs toolchain
route.alt: A common pivot from support, QA or journalism.

name: Dietitian
blurb: The regulated clinical nutrition profession, evidence-based, automation-resistant and private-practice friendly, with a modest NHS ceiling.

route.summary: Dietetics degree → HCPC registration → practise.
steps: NHS bands, industry or private practice
route.alt: Postgraduate dietetics conversion for science graduates.

name: Speech & language therapist
blurb: Highly relational, deeply automation-resistant rehabilitation work with private options, a capped ceiling the trade-off for the meaning.

route.summary: SLT degree → HCPC registration → practise.
route.alt: Postgraduate conversion route for relevant graduates.

name: Podiatrist
blurb: A hands-on clinical foot-health profession with strong private-practice earnings and ownership, an under-the-radar, durable choice.

route.summary: Podiatry degree → HCPC registration → NHS or private practice.
steps: NHS, or build and own a private clinic
route.alt: Advanced practice (podiatric surgery) raises the ceiling.

name: Dental hygienist
blurb: Skilled, hands-on preventive dental care with good hours and steady private demand, a shorter, cheaper route than dentistry.

route.summary: Dental hygiene/therapy diploma or degree → GDC registration.
steps: Diploma or BSc in dental hygiene/therapy
NHS or private practices; often flexible/part-time
route.alt: Many enter after working as a dental nurse.

name: Pharmacy technician
blurb: A regulated, accessible healthcare role supporting pharmacists, secure and in demand, with a clear stepping stone toward pharmacy.

route.summary: Level 3 apprenticeship → GPhC registration.
steps: Specialist roles, or study toward pharmacist
route.alt: A common route into pharmacy or wider healthcare science.

name: Counsellor
blurb: Trusted talking-therapy work you can practise independently, deeply automation-resistant, but income is modest and often part-time early on.

route.summary: Accredited counselling training + placement hours → accreditation.
steps: BACP/NCPS accreditation → private or agency work
route.alt: Overlaps with psychotherapy; NHS talking-therapy roles exist.

name: Financial adviser (IFA)
blurb: Advises clients on money and investments, with strong commission upside and the option to build your own practice, regulated and relationship-driven.

route.summary: Level 4 Diploma → adviser under an authorised firm → build a client book.
steps: Level 4 Diploma for Regulated Financial Planning
Build a client bank, or set up your own practice
route.alt: Chartered status (Level 6) raises fees and credibility.

name: Tax adviser
blurb: A technical, well-paid specialism advising on tax, durable expertise with strong private-practice potential, and a real exam gauntlet.

route.summary: Degree/AAT → tax trainee → ATT then CTA qualifications.
steps: Trainee at a firm; any degree or AAT
route.alt: A common crossover from accountancy.

name: Compliance officer
blurb: Keeps regulated firms on the right side of the rules, secure, rising demand, and well-paid in financial services, if procedural by nature.

route.summary: Degree → compliance/analyst role → industry qualifications.
steps: Compliance manager → head of compliance / MLRO
route.alt: A common move from audit, legal or operations.

name: Insurance broker
blurb: Arranges cover and advises clients on risk, with commission upside and brokerage-ownership potential, relationship-driven and cyclical.

route.summary: Any background → trainee broker → CII qualifications.
steps: Trainee broker; no specific degree needed
Account executive → own book or brokerage
route.alt: Overlaps with underwriting and financial advice.

name: Legal executive (CILEX)
blurb: A lower-debt route into qualified legal practice, earn while you train, specialise in one area, and reach solicitor-equivalent work over time.

route.summary: CILEX qualifications while working → Chartered Legal Executive.
steps: CILEX Professional Qualification alongside a legal job
Specialise; can cross to solicitor via a reduced route
route.alt: A debt-free alternative to the traditional solicitor path.

name: Prison officer
blurb: Demanding, people-centred public service with strong security and a pension, automation-proof, but stressful and physically confronting.

route.summary: Apply → vetting + fitness → paid initial training.
steps: Online tests, interview, fitness and security vetting
route.alt: No degree required; wide entry.

name: Probation officer
blurb: Manages offenders in the community, meaningful, secure public-sector work with heavy caseloads and emotional demands.

route.summary: Professional Qualification in Probation (degree-level) → practise.
steps: Senior probation officer, or specialist units
route.alt: Probation services officer roles as a lower-entry start.

name: Diplomat (Foreign Office)
blurb: Represents the UK abroad across policy, trade and crisis work, prestigious, varied and secure, but fiercely competitive and posting-driven.

route.summary: Diplomatic Fast Stream → postings at home and overseas.
route.alt: Direct-entry policy and specialist roles at the FCDO.

name: Intelligence analyst
blurb: Turns data and information into assessments for security, government or business, analytical, clearance-gated and durable, if secretive by nature.

route.summary: Degree + analytical skills → analyst role → security clearance.
steps: Any analytical discipline; languages or CS help
route.alt: Crossover from data analysis, the military or policing.

name: Environmental health officer
blurb: Protects public health across food, housing and safety, a stable, varied, meaningful regulatory profession with steady local-authority demand.

route.summary: Accredited degree → registration → practise.
route.alt: A degree apprenticeship route is emerging.

name: Chemical engineer
blurb: Designs the processes behind fuels, pharmaceuticals and materials, among the best-paid engineering fields, with strong energy-transition demand.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate scheme → chartership (CEng).
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships at major process employers.

name: Biomedical engineer
blurb: Designs medical devices and clinical technology, a growing field blending engineering and healthcare, durable against automation.

route.summary: Accredited degree → graduate role → chartership.
steps: Device manufacturer, NHS clinical engineering or research
route.alt: NHS Scientist Training Programme (clinical engineering).

name: Robotics engineer
blurb: Builds autonomous systems across manufacturing, logistics and defence, a high-growth field fusing mechanical, electrical and software skills.

route.summary: Engineering/CS degree → robotics role → specialise.
steps: Control, perception or ML; often an MSc
route.alt: Strong overlap with ML engineering and controls.

name: Quantity surveyor
blurb: Manages construction costs and contracts, a stable, chartered, well-paid profession riding sustained UK infrastructure demand.

route.summary: RICS-accredited degree (or apprenticeship) → APC → MRICS.
steps: Structured APC training with a contractor/consultancy
route.alt: Degree apprenticeships qualify with no tuition debt.

name: Geologist
blurb: Studies the earth for energy, water, mining and environmental work, fieldwork-rich and increasingly tied to the energy transition and geohazards.

route.summary: Geology degree (often MSc) → graduate role → chartership.
steps: Geology or earth science; MSc often expected
Consultancy, energy, water or environmental sectors
route.alt: Strong overlap with environmental and engineering geology.

name: Statistician
blurb: Designs studies and models uncertainty across government, pharma and research, durable, numerate and quietly in demand.

route.summary: Numerate degree → (often MSc) → statistician role.
steps: Maths, statistics or a quantitative science
An MSc in statistics is common
Government Statistical Service, pharma or research
route.alt: Strong crossover with data science and actuarial work.

name: Video editor
blurb: Shapes raw footage into finished stories, creative and freelance-friendly, but project-based income and AI-assisted editing are pressures.

route.summary: Showreel → assistant/junior editor → freelance or staff.
steps: Runner/assistant editor at a studio or agency
route.alt: Social-video demand is a fast, accessible entry point.

name: Animator
blurb: Brings characters and motion to life for film, games and advertising, highly creative, portfolio-driven, and increasingly AI-pressured at the routine end.

route.summary: Animation degree or self-taught portfolio → junior animator.
route.alt: Games, film and motion-graphics are distinct tracks.

name: Fashion designer
blurb: Designs garments and collections, intensely creative with brand-ownership upside, but low pay early, insecure, and fiercely competitive.

route.summary: Fashion degree + portfolio → junior designer → build a name.
steps: Fashion design degree; a strong portfolio
Senior designer, or launch your own label
route.alt: Internships and competitions are key to breaking in.

name: Industrial / product designer
blurb: Designs physical products where form meets engineering, creative and better-paid than pure graphic design, with consultancy and startup routes.

route.summary: Product/industrial design degree + portfolio → junior designer.
steps: Industrial or product design degree; a CAD portfolio
Junior designer at a consultancy or manufacturer
Senior designer → design lead, or own studio
route.alt: Overlaps with UX and mechanical engineering.

name: PR manager
blurb: Shapes reputation and media coverage for brands and people, fast-paced and relationship-driven, with agency-ownership upside and AI pressure on routine output.

route.summary: Any degree → PR/comms role → build a track record.
steps: Media relationships, campaigns, a results record
Account director → head of comms, or own agency
route.alt: CIPR qualifications and journalism crossovers help.

name: Translator
blurb: Converts meaning across languages, flexible and independent, but machine translation is reshaping the field, pushing value toward specialist and literary work.

route.summary: Fluency + translation qualification → freelance or in-house.
steps: Degree or diploma in translation; near-native fluency
Legal, medical, technical or literary niche
route.alt: CIOL/ITI membership and specialism resist automation best.

name: Roofer
blurb: A physical, weather-exposed construction trade with steady demand and strong self-employment earnings, a lower ceiling and real bodily toll the trade-offs.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ → roofer (→ self-employed).
route.alt: Specialising (leadwork, heritage) raises rates.

name: Plasterer
blurb: A skilled finishing trade with consistent demand and good self-employed rates, hard on the body, with a capped ceiling.

route.summary: Apprenticeship → NVQ → plasterer (→ self-employed).
steps: Domestic/commercial work, or a small firm
route.alt: Specialist finishes and dry-lining raise earnings.

name: Landscape gardener
blurb: Outdoor, hands-on and highly automation-proof, with easy self-employment, modest pay and seasonal, weather-dependent work the trade-offs.

route.summary: Apprenticeship/short course → experience → self-employment.
steps: Experience across soft and hard landscaping
Build a client base; design-and-build for higher rates
route.alt: Garden design qualifications lift the ceiling.

name: HGV driver
blurb: Keeps supply chains moving, with a persistent shortage propping up pay, but long hours away from home, and automation a long-horizon question.

route.summary: Licence acquisition → Driver CPC → HGV driver.
steps: Category C/C+E licence training and test
Employed haulier; specialise (ADR, tankers) for more pay
route.alt: Employer-funded training schemes are common.

name: Hairdresser
blurb: A creative, personal, automation-proof trade with strong self-employment and salon-ownership routes, low early pay and physical strain the costs.

route.summary: Apprenticeship/NVQ → stylist → chair rental or own salon.
steps: Grow a client base as an employed stylist
Rent a chair, go mobile, or open a salon
route.alt: Barbering and specialisms (colour) raise earnings.

name: Baker
blurb: A hands-on craft trade with artisan and business upside, early starts, physical work and modest pay the trade-offs for the independence.

route.summary: Entry role or apprenticeship → baker → own bakery.
steps: Bakery role or a food/baking apprenticeship
Craft techniques; artisan or production focus
Head baker, or open a bakery or market stall
route.alt: Culinary college and patisserie specialisms raise the ceiling.

name: Operations manager
blurb: Runs the day-to-day machinery of a business, a broad, promotable role reached by experience, with strong progression into senior leadership.

route.summary: Experience in a function → team lead → operations management.
steps: Experience in a core function (logistics, service, production)
route.alt: An MBA or ops apprenticeships accelerate the climb.

name: Supply chain manager
blurb: Orchestrates the flow of goods from source to customer, strategically important, well-paid, and increasingly data- and resilience-driven.

route.summary: Degree or graduate scheme → analyst → supply chain manager.
steps: Supply chain/logistics analyst or graduate scheme
CIPS procurement or supply chain certifications
route.alt: Common progression from procurement or operations.
